:::{#thm-eigenvectors-independent}
#### Eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent

If $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k$ are eigenvectors of a $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$
for eigenvalues $\eigval_1, \ldots, \eigval_k$ that are all different,
then $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_k$ are linearly independent (@def-linearly-independent).

:::

::: proof

By [induction](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-proof-by-induction) on $k$.
For $k = 1$, $\vecf{v}_1 \ne \vzero$ is linearly independent on its own.
Suppose the result holds for $k - 1$ eigenvectors, and
$\sumto{i}{k} c_i \vecf{v}_i = \vzero$. Then

$$
\ba
\vzero
&= (\matr{A} - \eigval_k \matr{I}_p) \sumto{i}{k} c_i \vecf{v}_i
&& \text{(multiply the supposed equation by } \matr{A} - \eigval_k \matr{I}_p \text{)}
\\
&= \sumto{i}{k} c_i\,(\matr{A} - \eigval_k \matr{I}_p)\,\vecf{v}_i
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-linear)}
\\
&= \sumto{i}{k} c_i\,(\eigval_i - \eigval_k)\,\vecf{v}_i
&& \text{(@thm-eigen-shift-power, part 1, with } s = -\eigval_k \text{)}
\\
&= \sumto{i}{k-1} c_i\,(\eigval_i - \eigval_k)\,\vecf{v}_i.
&& \text{(the } i = k \text{ term is } \vzero \text{)}
\ea
$$

By the induction hypothesis $\vecf{v}_1, \ldots, \vecf{v}_{k-1}$ are linearly independent,
so every $c_i\,(\eigval_i - \eigval_k) = 0$ for $i < k$,
and since $\eigval_i \ne \eigval_k$, every $c_i = 0$ for $i < k$.
The supposed equation then reads $c_k \vecf{v}_k = \vzero$ with $\vecf{v}_k \ne \vzero$,
so $c_k = 0$ too.

:::
